summary: CR-109 code review + unit tests uncover TWO critical wiring bugs. Dynamic prep-time computation and auto-accept behaviour are effectively DEAD CODE — they will never trigger for the real API payload. Login/dashboard/regressions all fine; webpack compiles clean. Popup itself cannot be live-tested (no fOrderStatus=0/7 orders in preprod).

integration_issues.issue: computeAggregatorPrepTime() looks for bracket fields `min_items` / `max_items` / `bonus_minutes` but the actual restaurant settings payload (per task spec + preprod for rid=478) uses `min` / `max` / `bonus`. Result: bracket lookup never matches → function always returns basePrepTime (15) regardless of item count.

integration_issues.flow: CR-109 settings surface for auto-accept + prep-time bracket
integration_issues.issue: profileTransform.js `fromAPI.settings()` (L325-376) does NOT expose `default_prep_time`, `prep_time_bonus_config`, or `auto_prep_time_ack` on the `settings` object returned by useRestaurant(). It only emits camelCase `defaultPrepTime` (no bracket config, no auto-accept flag). But AggregatorOrderPopOut.jsx reads them via snake_case: L59 `settings?.auto_prep_time_ack`, and computeAggregatorPrepTime reads `settings.default_prep_time` + `settings.prep_time_bonus_config`. All three come back as undefined. Consequences: (a) `autoAcceptEnabled` is ALWAYS false — even if a tenant had `auto_prep_time_ack=Yes`, the 1.5s auto-accept effect would never fire; (b) `computedPrepTime` is always 15 (base fallback); (c) pre-select pill always defaults to 15-min pill instead of the bracket-derived value. Verified live via React fiber walk of RestaurantContext.Provider value on rid=478: settings keys = [isCoupon, isLoyalty, isCustomerWallet, aggregatorAutoKot, autoKot, autoBill, defaultPrepTime, confirmOrderTone, aggregatorOrderTone, useToken, showScanPopup]. No prep_time_bonus_config, no auto_prep_time_ack.

unit_test_results.conclusion: Only the base-prep-time fallback works. All bracket-based computations fail because of field-name mismatch (min_items vs min etc).

action_items: FIX #1 (utils/aggregatorPrepTime.js L24-28): Read bracket fields as `b.min` / `b.max` / `b.bonus` (or accept both variants) to match the actual API/config shape per CR-109 spec.

FIX #2 (api/transforms/profileTransform.js settings transform L325-376): Expose the three new keys on the settings object so useRestaurant() consumers can read them. Options: (a) add snake_case pass-through: `default_prep_time`, `prep_time_bonus_config`, `auto_prep_time_ack`; OR (b) map to camelCase and update AggregatorOrderPopOut + aggregatorPrepTime util to read camelCase keys (defaultPrepTime already exists as camelCase — reuse). Recommend option (b) for consistency with rest of transform.

After fixes: re-verify with a simulated order (fOrderStatus=0/7, items qty=5) that pill 20-min gets pre-selected, and toggle auto_prep_time_ack=Yes on a test tenant to confirm 1500ms auto-accept fires exactly once (autoAcceptFiredRef Set dedupe works).
critical_code_review_comments: aggregatorPrepTime.js util contract mismatch with API payload — silently degrades to base prep time; no defensive log/warning to catch this in prod.

profileTransform.settings() is the single source of truth for the settings context — any new CR that adds settings-driven behaviour MUST add the field here, otherwise consumers read undefined. Consider adding a smoke assertion / snapshot test.

AggregatorOrderPopOut auto-accept effect deps include `handleAccept` (a useCallback that itself depends on many values). If `effectivePrepTime` changes between renders (e.g. staff edits pill after popup shows but before 1.5s elapses), the effect will re-schedule. Deduplication via autoAcceptFiredRef.current.has(order.orderId) protects against double-accept — OK, but the timer from the previous render is cancelled by cleanup — so behaviour is fine. No change needed once main bugs fixed.

Line 92 useEffect deps: `[currentIndex, queue.length, computedPrepTime]` — should also include `queue` identity or use `order?.orderId` to be robust against orders swapping without index change (edge case).

rca of the issue: CR-109 introduces a util + effect that read three settings keys (default_prep_time, prep_time_bonus_config, auto_prep_time_ack) directly off the `settings` object returned by useRestaurant(). But the profileTransform layer between the API and the context has always exposed only a curated camelCase surface — none of these three keys are in that surface. Additionally the util was written against a hypothetical bracket schema (min_items/max_items/bonus_minutes) rather than the actual schema (min/max/bonus) confirmed in the CR spec. Two independent oversights that together render CR-109 inert in production. Repro: (1) node run of unit tests shows bracket lookup fails; (2) React fiber walk on live dashboard shows settings object lacks all 3 keys.
